spans.s:
Phaṇa occurs in some manuscripts of the kauṣītaki upaniṣad, and is explained as meaning an ‘ornament.’ But it is merely a misreading of the correct word phala in the compound phalahastāḥ, ‘bearing fruits in their hands.’
Foot notes i. 4. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 398; Keith, śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka, 19, n. 1.

Phāṇṭa in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa is said to denote the first particles of butter produced by churning, ‘creamy butter.’
Foot notes iii. 1, 3, 8. Cf. Eggeling, Sacred Books of the East, 26, 14, n. 1.
